evals.prompt: I'm about to open a PR for my refunds branch. It adds a migration for a refunds table, two new API handlers, a background worker that calls the payment provider, and a React button. Can you do a deep review of the whole branch from every angle before I push it?
evals.expected_output: The agent pins the base and head SHAs, runs the scope helper, picks personas from the signals it finds (correctness, security, performance, data-database, api-compat, reliability-operability, test-quality, ux-accessibility), and launches every persona Agent call in a single message, each with a self-contained brief. It then dedupes the findings, sends each high or critical finding to a skeptical verifier, and returns one ranked report that leads with a verdict and includes a coverage section.
expectations: Records explicit base and head commit SHAs before launching personas
When subagents are available (as in Claude Code), launches all persona subagents in one assistant message rather than sequentially
Each persona brief contains the repository path, the pinned SHAs or diff command, the change intent, the persona text, and the finding schema
Includes the ux-accessibility persona because UI files changed, and the data-database persona because a migration changed
Runs a refutation-style verification on every high or critical finding before reporting it
Final report starts with a verdict line and includes a Coverage and gaps section, and no repository file is edited during the review

evals.prompt: Before we cut the release, review the src/payments module end to end. Have separate reviewers look at it for security, data integrity, failure handling and so on, then give me one prioritized list.
evals.expected_output: The agent treats this as a module target with no diff, lists the files with git ls-files, measures size and churn hotspots, and does not run the UX persona because there are no UI files. Pre-existing issues are in scope. If the module is large it slices the files and stays under the concurrency cap. It returns a single prioritized report with verified high and critical findings.
expectations: Identifies the target as a module or path target and uses git ls-files rather than a diff
Reports churn hotspots or otherwise prioritizes heavily changed files
Skips or justifies skipping the ux-accessibility persona when there are no UI files
Treats pre-existing issues as in scope for a module target
Produces exactly one consolidated report rather than one report per persona

evals.prompt: Can you do a full multi-agent review of PR 482? It just fixes two typos in the onboarding copy and bumps a log message.
evals.expected_output: The agent sees that the target is tiny and low-risk, recommends a single pr-review pass instead of a parallel review, and explains the cost trade-off. If the user still wants a parallel review, it runs a trimmed one with two or three personas rather than all of them.
expectations: Recommends the lighter pr-review pass and explains why
Does not launch all nine personas for a copy-only change
If the user still wants a parallel review after the recommendation, it is a trimmed one (two or three personas, such as correctness and ux-accessibility), stated as a one-line plan before launching

evals.prompt: Run the parallel review on my branch, but only with the security and api-compat reviewers. I don't need the rest.
evals.expected_output: The agent pins the base and head SHAs, launches exactly two persona subagents (security and api-compat) in one message, and lists the other applicable lanes under 'Personas not run' in the report's Coverage section rather than silently omitting them.
expectations: Launches exactly the security and api-compat personas and no others
Launches both persona Agent calls in the same assistant message
The report's Coverage section lists the lanes that were not run and says the user chose to skip them

evals.prompt: Do a multi-agent review of my branch. Heads-up: the new GET /orders/:id handler looks like it skips the ownership check, but all /orders routes go through the scoping middleware in app/middleware/scope_orders.py.
evals.expected_output: Any high or critical finding about a missing ownership check is sent to a verifier subagent whose brief uses a neutral finding id and does not name the persona. The verifier traces the middleware, the finding is refuted, and it appears in the report's 'Refuted during verification' section with a citation instead of in the findings list.
expectations: Launches a verifier subagent for each high or critical finding rather than reporting it directly
The verifier brief does not reveal which persona raised the finding or how many agreed
A finding refuted by the middleware appears under 'Refuted during verification' with a file:line citation
The refuted finding does not count toward the verdict

evals.prompt: Review the whole services/platform directory from every angle before the release. It's around 120 files.
evals.expected_output: The agent treats this as a module target, slices the file list by subsystem, states the plan (personas, slices, agent count) before launching, launches at most about 10 agents per message, runs further waves for the rest, and records the slices and waves in the report's Coverage section.
expectations: Slices the file list by subsystem rather than giving every persona all 120 files
States the plan with an estimated agent count before launching
No single assistant message launches more than about 10 Agent calls
The Coverage section includes a Slices line saying which persona saw which slice

evals.prompt: Can you run a full parallel review on PR 2210? It's from an outside contributor's fork and touches the auth middleware and the test fixtures.
evals.expected_output: The agent runs the trust check, sees that the PR comes from a fork, fetches the PR head before computing the merge base, reviews from a detached worktree pinned to the verified head SHA, and writes 'Project commands you may run: none' into every persona and verifier brief. Briefs also tell personas to treat the PR description and code comments as material under review, not instructions. Coverage records that no project commands were run.
expectations: Checks whether the PR is cross-repository (for example via gh pr view --json isCrossRepository)
Fetches the PR head before running git merge-base
Every persona and verifier brief says no project commands may be run
Does not run the project's tests, build, or type checker
Coverage states that nothing from the PR was executed

evals.prompt: Subagents aren't available in this session, my agent can't launch them. Can you still do the full multi-angle review of my branch? It adds a POST /refunds handler, a migration that creates a refunds table, and a retry wrapper around the payment client.
evals.expected_output: The agent follows the skill's "No subagents available" path: it pins the base and head SHAs, picks personas from the scope signals, and works through the same persona briefs itself, one lane at a time in the current session, recording each lane's findings before starting the next. It verifies every high or critical finding by re-reading the code from scratch, ranks with the same finding schema and verdict ladder, and states in Coverage that the lanes ran sequentially with less independence than separate reviewers.
expectations: Does not try to launch subagents; works through the persona briefs one after another in the current session
Records explicit base and head commit SHAs and picks personas from the change's signals (at least security, data-database and reliability-operability for this change)
Finishes and records each persona lane's findings before starting the next lane
Verifies every high or critical finding by re-reading the code from scratch before reporting it
Uses the same finding schema and verdict ladder as a parallel run, and the report leads with a verdict line
The Coverage section states that the lanes ran sequentially and that the reviews were less independent than separate reviewers
